title: OpenSpec epic: stabilize-release-trust-signals
description:
OpenSpec change: `stabilize-release-trust-signals`

Goals:
- Stabilize release pipeline execution so publishing is deterministic and CI-resolvable.
- Establish repository trust baseline (license visibility, metadata quality, valid docs links, project-accurate automation guidance).
- Guarantee future release artifact visibility (one `v<lockstep-version>` tag + one matching GitHub release), with future-only guarantees and no historical backfill requirement.

Scope:
- Capabilities covered: `release-pipeline-reliability`, `repository-trust-baseline`, `release-artifact-visibility`.
- Includes required and optional dependency mapping from OpenSpec tasks/design.
- Excludes unrelated engine/runtime refactors.
acceptance_criteria:
AC1: all ADDED requirements in release-pipeline-reliability, repository-trust-baseline, and release-artifact-visibility are implemented and validated.
AC2: release workflow behavior matches OpenSpec success, skip, and failure scenarios.
AC3: trust baseline artifacts/docs are present and verifiable.
AC4: openspec validate stabilize-release-trust-signals --strict passes after implementation.
notes: 2026-02-12 validation run passed: release prereq check, missing-prereq negative-path check, artifact-coupling validation, turbo build/lint/test, and openspec strict validation. Epic remains in_progress for review-driven closure.
close_reason: Review complete: AC1-AC4 verified against implementation and passing validations

title: Release pipeline: make publish toolchain explicit and CI-resolvable
description:
OpenSpec refs:
- Capability: `release-pipeline-reliability`
- Requirement: "Publish Toolchain Is Explicit And CI-Resolvable"
- Scenarios:
  - "Publish command runs with declared tools"
  - "Missing publish prerequisite blocks release early"

Expected outputs:
- Root publish command chain uses explicit CLI resolution (`npm exec` or equivalent).
- Root workspace toolchain declares required release CLIs (`@changesets/cli`, `turbo`).
- Missing tool checks fail before versioning/publish side effects.

Validation/tests:
- CI-like command flow runs without `command not found` failures.
- Missing-tool path fails before `changeset version`/publish side effects.

Success criteria:
- Toolchain behavior matches both referenced scenarios.
acceptance_criteria:
AC1: publish-packages resolves required CLIs explicitly via npm exec (or equivalent explicit resolution).
AC2: required release CLIs @changesets/cli and turbo are declared at the root toolchain boundary.
AC3: missing CLI prerequisite fails before versioning/publish side effects.
AC4: missing-tool behavior is validated via scripted negative-path CI-like execution (not ad hoc manual checks).

title: Release pipeline: enforce adapter gating and no-changeset no-op
description:
OpenSpec refs:
- Capability: `release-pipeline-reliability`
- Requirements:
  - "Release Remains Gated By Adapter CI Results"
  - "No-Changeset Path Is Safe"
- Scenarios:
  - "Both adapter CI workflows succeed"
  - "One adapter CI workflow is skipped or fails"
  - "No pending changesets"

Expected outputs:
- `.github/workflows/main-release.yml` enforces adapter CI gating as specified.
- No-changeset path remains publish/tag/release no-op.

Validation/tests:
- Success path proceeds only when both adapter workflows are `success`.
- Skipped/failed adapter result blocks release.
- No changesets skip publish/tag/release steps.

Success criteria:
- Workflow control flow matches referenced scenarios.
acceptance_criteria:
AC1: release publishes only when Node and Browser adapters are both success.
AC2: any skipped or failed adapter result blocks publish.
AC3: no pending .changeset files triggers no-op publish/tag/release path.

comments.author: Mark Wotton
comments.text: Verified ACs against .github/workflows/main-release.yml: (AC1) release job requires both needs.node.result and needs.browser.result == success before publish path, (AC2) skipped and non-success adapter results hard-fail in Verify CI results step, (AC3) has_changesets=false when no .changeset/*.md and all publish-path steps are guarded with if: steps.changesets.outputs.has_changesets == 'true'. Validation run: npm run release:check-prereqs (pass), npm run release:validate-missing-prereq (pass, expected negative path). No workflow code change required for this task.

title: Release artifacts: create lockstep tag and GitHub release
description:
OpenSpec refs:
- Capability: `release-artifact-visibility`
- Requirements:
  - "Successful Publish Produces Version Artifacts"
  - "Historical Backfill Is Out Of Scope By Default"
- Scenarios:
  - "Publish with new version succeeds"
  - "Existing historical versions are present before rollout"

Expected outputs:
- Successful lockstep publish creates exactly one `v<lockstep-version>` tag.
- Successful lockstep publish creates exactly one matching GitHub release.
- Future-only guarantee implemented (no historical backfill automation).

Validation/tests:
- Validate success path artifact creation.
- Validate no backfill implementation is introduced.

Success criteria:
- Artifact generation follows selected namespace and future-only scope.
acceptance_criteria:
AC1: one v<lockstep-version> tag is created per successful lockstep publish.
AC2: one matching GitHub release is created per successful lockstep publish and is published (non-draft).
AC3: release notes content is sourced from changesets-generated changelog/release notes.
AC4: no historical artifact backfill automation is added.

title: Release artifacts: enforce post-publish coupling and failure semantics
description:
OpenSpec refs:
- Capability: `release-artifact-visibility`
- Requirement: "Artifact Generation Is Coupled To Successful Publish"
- Scenarios:
  - "Publish step fails"
  - "No pending changesets"
  - "Artifact generation fails after publish"

Expected outputs:
- Artifact generation runs only post-publish success.
- Skip and failure behavior is explicit and enforced.

Validation/tests:
- Confirm no artifacts are created when publish fails or is skipped.
- Confirm artifact-generation failure fails workflow with clear error.

Success criteria:
- Coupling/failure/skip behavior matches all referenced scenarios.
acceptance_criteria:
AC1: no artifacts are created when publish fails.
AC2: no artifacts are created when no changesets are pending.
AC3: artifact-generation error after publish fails workflow.
AC4: skip/failure semantics are validated in a sandboxed GitHub Actions run path (test branch/fork) that avoids production side effects.
